key_insight: This paper shows that reinforcement learning can still improve LLMs even when there is no ground-truth answer, by using deterministic execution feedback as a verifiable learning signal. The proposed RiVER framework turns score-based tasks into trainable objectives without requiring labeled solutions.
problem_solved: Many RL methods for LLMs depend on known ground-truth answers to compute rewards, which limits them to tasks with clear correct outputs. This work addresses how to train models on tasks where the final solution is unknown but execution or scoring feedback is still available.
method: Introduce RiVER: a ranking-induced verifiable framework for learning from score-based optimization tasks without ground-truth solutions.
Use deterministic execution feedback as continuous-valued supervision instead of binary correct/incorrect labels.
Apply group-relative reinforcement learning to optimize model outputs using relative rankings among candidate solutions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this expands reinforcement learning beyond problems with explicit labels, enabling training on a broader set of real-world optimization tasks. It makes LLM improvement more practical in settings where only execution-based signals or scores are available.

paper_title: Reinforcement Learning without Ground-Truth Solutions can Improve LLMs
paper_authors: Yingyu Lin, Qiyue Gao, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Xunpeng Huang, Kun Zhou
